newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot propane slides with U.S. warm up.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot propane slides with U.S. warm up.

text.p: Canada propane prices declined sharply over the past week or so, moving in the opposite direction to temperatures south of the border, traders said.
In the western Canadian hub of Edmonton, spot propane prices were assessed at between 55.0 and 60.0 cents a gallon on Thursday, down from 80/90 cents in the end December period.

"It's tracking the southern markets," said a Calgary trader. "Conway is the biggest factor," he said, referring to sharply lower prices in the Midwest hub which had jumped amid an Arctic freeze there in early December.
In the eastern Canadian hub of Sarnia, spot propane prices also were lower, with the market pegged at about 63.50 cents a gallon mid-price, down from the mid to high 70s in late December.

The propane market south of the border was volatile on Thursday, with Conway prices trading a 65-75 cents range and ending in the middle, though that was sharply down from recent highs of nearly a $1 a gallon.

Recent cold weather drew in imports from Canada to the U.S., reflected in Thursday's American Petroleum Institute figures showing imports to the MidWest and Rocky Mountain regions of 122,000 barrels per day in the week ended December 27, about twice the level at the same time a year earlier.
Meanwhile, in the butane markets, field butane for Edmonton delivery also was lower by about 15 pct from late December at 40/45 cents a gallon, influenced by the weaker prices at Bellvieu, Texas.
